what: What Ring records on its own when a flood sensor gets wet, with Watermark off: the controlled test with my real devices

devices.sensor: Ring Flood & Freeze Sensor (2nd Gen), 'Water Heater', on Amazon Sidewalk
devices.camera: Ring Indoor Cam (2nd Gen), 'Flood Cam', aimed at the dish holding the sensor, motion detection on (default settings)

procedure: Water poured slowly into a flat dish holding the sensor, from outside the camera's view. Water left standing for 3 minutes. The phone's screen was recorded throughout over USB; notifications were read from the phone's notification log with their post times.
flood_alert_text: Home Water Heater reported water at 10/22/26 08:35 PM

other_camera_events_that_day.cause: me pouring into the bowl on the first attempt (the sensor did not detect water: it was not sitting flat in a rounded bowl)

chime_alerts_for_sensor: not offered: the Chime's Audio Settings > Chime Alerts list contains only the Flood Cam, and the Chime's own screen reads 'Chime Alerts: Unavailable'
camera_linking_to_sensor: not offered: the Flood Cam's Linked Devices suggests only doorbells and smart lighting; the sensor's Linked Chimes page has nothing to link
evidence: Screenshots and phone screen recordings kept locally (demo/broll/ring-app/, not committed: they show my account)
